Cancelling a run that is already terminal returns `400`. Ownership is enforced server side; a cr

operations.name: Cancel a batch
operations.description: Moves the batch to `cancelling`; it becomes `cancelled` once running items stop. Completed items stay in the output file and are billed. Cancelling a cancelled or cancelling batch returns it unchanged.

operations.name: Fetch url context
operations.description: Fetch Markdown, HTML, links, highlights, and page metadata for 1 to 50 URLs, and optionally score each page with criteria. The response has one result per input URL, in input order. Check each result's status.type for per-URL failures. See the [Context API quickstart](/docs/context/quickstart), [Formats & Freshness](/docs/context/formats-and-freshness), and [Score Pages with Criteria](/docs/contex

urls.description: 1 to 50 http or https URLs. Your usage tier can lower the maximum. A string that is not an absolute http or https URL does not fail the request: its result has status.type invalid_url.

formats.description: What to return besides metadata, which is always returned for a page with content. highlights requires the highlights object. [] returns metadata only.

highlights.description: Highlights settings. Required when formats includes highlights, and allowed only then.

if_modified_since.description: A metadata.last_modified value from an earlier response, in IMF-fixdate form such as Thu, 03 Dec 1992 08:37:20 GMT. Requires exactly one URL and max_age_seconds 0. If the page has not changed since then, its result has status.type not_modified and no content, so keep the content you already have.

max_age_seconds.description: Maximum age of a stored copy to accept, up to 63072000 (two years). 0 always fetches the page live.

cache_only.description: When true, answer only from stored copies at most max_age_seconds old and never fetch live. A URL without one has status.type no_content. Requires max_age_seconds above 0.

timeout_ms.description: Time budget for fetching the pages. URLs are fetched in parallel, and a URL that does not finish in time has status.type crawl_timeout while the rest keep their content. The response can take slightly longer than this budget. With criteria, the maximum is 95000, and scoring may add up to 15 seconds.

criteria.description: Decision questions to score each page with, keyed by question ID. 1 to 5 questions. IDs must match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}, and query is reserved. Scoring never filters, reorders, or drops results.

operations.name: Create contextualized embeddings (v1)
operations.description: Generate contextualized embeddings for document chunks. Chunks from the same document share context awareness, improving retrieval quality for document-based applications.

input.description: Nested array structure where each inner array contains chunks from a single document. Chunks within the same document are encoded with document-level context awareness. Maximum 512 documents. Total chunks across all documents must not exceed 16,000. Total tokens per document must not exceed 32K. All chunks in a single request must not exceed 120,000 tokens combined. Empty strings are not allowed.

model.description: The contextualized embedding model to use

dimensions.description: Number of dimensions for output embeddings (Matryoshka). Range: 128-1024 for pplx-embed-context-v1-0.6b, 128-2560 for pplx-embed-context-v1-4b. Defaults to full dimensions (1024 or 2560).

encoding_format.description: Output encoding format for embeddings. base64_int8 returns base64-encoded signed int8 values. base64_binary returns base64-encoded packed binary (1 bit per dimension).

For requests that specify model or models without an effort level, the default is 1. Set max_steps to at least 3 when using finance_search with a direct model so the agent has enough steps to initialize and run the tool. Must be >= 1 if specified. Maximum allowed is 500.

model.description: Model ID in provider/model format (e.g., "openai/gpt-5.6-terra", "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5"). If models is also provided, models takes precedence. Required if neither models nor effort is provided.

models.description: Model fallback chain. Each model is in provider/model format. Models are tried in order until one succeeds. Max 5 models allowed. If set, takes precedence over single model field. The response.model will reflect the model that actually succeeded.

effort.description: Effort to run, as `name`, `name@latest`, or `name@` (e.g., "fast", "low", "fast@2026-09-29.0"). An effort level is a pre-configured model with system prompt and search parameters. `name` and `name@latest` run the active version. `name@` runs that exact version. An `effort` value returned on a response pins that configuration only when it carries a version. A returned value without a version runs t

profile.description: Saved, versioned configuration to run with. The version is resolved when the request is admitted. Cannot be combined with effort.

previous_response_id.description: OpenAI-compatible previous response id for multi-turn response chains. When set, the new response continues from the completed prior response's saved state. The prior response must belong to the same account and have completed.

prompt_cache_key.description: Stable key for prompt cache affinity. Send the same key on requests that share a prompt prefix, including retries and multi-turn conversations, so later requests can read the cached prefix. The key is scoped to your account and does not affect model routing. See [Prompt Caching](/docs/agent-api/prompt-caching).

prompt_cache_options.description: Prompt cache options. `implicit` (default) keeps the default cache breakpoints and provider automatic caching. `explicit` turns both off, so only `input_text` parts marked with `prompt_cache_breakpoint` are cached; with no marks, the request makes no cache writes. See [Prompt Caching](/docs/agent-api/prompt-caching).

response_format.description: Specifies the desired output format for the model response

store.description: OpenAI-compatible storage toggle. When false, the response is hidden from later retrieve calls, and the echoed response reports `store: false`. It can still be used as a `previous_response_id` continuation source.

stream.description: If true, returns SSE stream instead of JSON

tool_choice.description: Tool choice strategy. Use `{"type":"image_search"}` to force image search.

Requests with skills run on the durable backend and skills are not echoed back on Response objects.

temperature.description: OpenAI-compatible sampling temperature forwarded to generation.

top_p.description: OpenAI-compatible nucleus sampling parameter forwarded to generation.

page_token.description: Opaque token from a previous response's `next_page_token`

operations.name: Pause a monitor
operations.description: Stops scheduled runs and keeps the monitor's state. A queued run is cancelled (it ends `skipped`); a run already running finishes. Pausing a paused monitor returns it unchanged.

operations.name: Resume a monitor
operations.description: Resumes scheduled runs and sets `next_run_at` from now. Missed runs are not replayed individually. Resuming a monitor that is not paused returns HTTP `409` with `invalid_state`. State has a 90-day retention period, so a long-paused monitor may establish a new baseline. The same active-monitor limit applies to creation and resuming. At the limit, HTTP `409` with `quota_exceeded` leaves the monitor

operations.name: Retrieve agent response
operations.description: Retrieve a response created earlier. Returns a JSON snapshot of the response. Only responses created with `store` omitted or `true` can be retrieved; `store: false` responses return a 404.

operations.name: Run a monitor now
operations.description: Queues a manual run and returns it at once with status `queued`. The run's `id` is the `run_id` of its `monitor.run.completed` event, and you can follow it with get run. A monitor has at most one run at a time: while one is queued or running, this returns 409 `run_in_progress` with that run's ID. A paused monitor returns 409 `invalid_state`.

operations.name: Search the web
operations.description: Returns ranked web results for one query, or for up to five queries in one request. The response is a list of results, not a generated answer.

query.description: One search query, or an array of 1 to 5 queries. Each query is 1 to 8192 bytes of UTF-8; the limit counts bytes, not characters. `max_results` applies to the combined results of all queries.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results in the response, across all queries in the request. 1 to 20 for `web` and `fast`, 1 to 50 for `people`.

search_type.description: Search type: `web` for general web search, `fast` for lower-latency web search, or `people` for people search. `max_results` above 20 is only supported for `people`.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, such as `US`. Returns results more relevant to that country.

search_language_filter.description: ISO 639-1 language codes, such as `en` or `fr`. Returns results in those languages. Up to 20 codes.

operations.name: Test a monitor's webhook
operations.description: Sends one signed `monitor.webhook.test` event to the configured webhook URL. Takes no request body and returns the delivery outcome after a response or a 10-second timeout. The test is not retried and does not count toward the `webhook_failing` pause threshold. A monitor without a webhook returns HTTP `409` with `invalid_state`.

operations.name: Update a monitor
operations.description: Replaces each top-level field the body names: any subset of `name`, `goal`, `targets`, `schedule`, `webhook` and `metadata`. An absent key leaves the field unchanged. `null` clears an optional field: `goal` becomes `""`, `metadata` becomes `{}`, `webhook` is removed; `null` for `name`, `targets` or `schedule` returns 400. An empty object returns the monitor unchanged. A new `schedule` recomputes `

targets.description: Exactly one `search` target, or 1 to 10 `page` targets with distinct URLs

operations.name: Add a skill revision
operations.description: Uploads a new zip bundle as a new revision of an existing skill. Pass the revision you expect to replace as the required `expected_revision`; the request fails with `409` if the skill has already moved past it, so the update cannot race a concurrent write. Name and description are re-read from the new bundle.

skill_id.description: Skill identifier returned by create or `GET /v1/skills`

expected_revision.description: Opaque revision token the skill must currently be at. The write applies only if it matches, so it cannot race a concurrent update.
